summary: A tool reference for Refero's MCP server, which gives an AI agent three research layers: styles for visual direction and taste, screens for concrete UI patterns, and flows for multi-step journeys. It lists each tool, its parameters, good example queries and how to search well, plus common mistakes and what to do when results are weak. Its key method is to search several visual angles, treat each returned style as an ingredient rather than a template, pick one primary foundation and borrow one or two details from others. For a design system it shows a research-first way to gather references before choosing tokens, while translating everything to the person's own product.
key_ideas: Refero research has three layers: styles (taste), screens (UI patterns), flows (journeys)
Search styles first for anything about visual direction, brand feel, type, color, layout or polish
Run 3-5 style searches from different angles: broad aesthetic, domain, and a known brand
Do not stop at the first good result; use later pages to find less obvious directions
Treat each style as a reference ingredient, not a template; never copy one style directly
Pick one primary foundation for mood and density and borrow 1-2 details from other styles
Extract layout, component, spacing and elevation rules, not only colors and fonts
Search screens by what is literally on the screen, using concrete UI terms
Styles currently cover web marketing and product pages, not dashboards, auth, settings or iOS screens
Use flows for journey logic such as onboarding, checkout, cancellation and password reset
When results are weak, broaden the query, drop adjectives, try adjacent categories or a known product

claims.claim: Styles currently focus on web marketing and product pages and do not cover in-app dashboards, auth screens, settings screens or iOS app screens as style systems.
Full styles are large, so the recommended maximum batch for refero_get_style is 3-4 IDs.
claims.evidence: refero_get_style parameters: recommended max batch is 3-4

claims.claim: refero_get_similar_screens takes an optional limit whose default is usually 10 and maximum usually 20.
claims.evidence: refero_get_similar_screens: Default is usually 10; max is usually 20

claims.claim: refero_get_screen_image returns image content and can use more context than text tools.
Flow IDs are numeric while style and screen IDs are UUIDs.

rules.rule: Search Refero styles first for any task involving visual direction, brand feel, typography, color, layout, spacing, elevation, components, imagery or polish.
rules.why: Styles are the layer for visual direction and taste.
rules.evidence: refero_search_styles: Use first for any task with visual direction

rules.rule: Run 3-5 style searches from different visual angles, including one broad aesthetic query, one domain or category query, and one known-brand query when relevant.
rules.why: Do not stop at the first good result.

rules.rule: Pick one style as the primary foundation for mood and density and borrow only 1-2 specific details from other styles.
rules.why: Each style is a reference ingredient, not a template.

rules.rule: Extract layout, component, spacing and elevation rules from a reference style, not only its colors and fonts.
rules.why: Listed in how to use returned styles.

rules.rule: Keep the source's token, component and imagery roles instead of repurposing them; use real, generated or stock assets, or an intentional art-directed placeholder when none is available.
rules.why: Preserve source roles and media roles.

rules.rule: Translate every borrowed reference to the user's product, audience and constraints; never copy a single style directly.
rules.evidence: Common Mistakes: Do not copy a single style directly

rules.rule: Write screen searches with concrete UI terms for what is literally on the screen (e.g. 'pricing page annual monthly toggle'), and search styles first when the query is aesthetic.
rules.why: Concrete terminology beats broad aesthetic words for screens.

rules.rule: Do not rely on screens as the main source of visual taste when styles are available.
rules.why: Styles are the taste layer; screens are for product-specific logic.

rules.rule: Do not assume Refero styles cover dashboards, auth screens, settings or iOS app screens; for those, use styles for taste and screens/flows for structure.
rules.why: Listed as a common mistake; current style coverage is web marketing and product pages.

rules.rule: Fetch at most 3-4 full styles per refero_get_style batch, and retry screen batches with fewer IDs if one fails.
Use refero_get_screen_image only when text metadata is not enough to judge a screen.
rules.why: Images use more context than text tools.

rules.rule: Do not pass limit, image_size or include_similar to search tools, or image_size/include_similar to refero_get_screen; use the dedicated image and similar-screens tools.
Do not use old _tool suffixed names or call get_design_guidance; use the styles, screens and flows tools.
When results are weak, broaden the query, remove adjectives, search adjacent categories, try a known product, inspect later pages, and for sparse flows rebuild the journey from related screens.
Call the Refero tools by the exact names the client shows (they carry the refero_ prefix, possibly namespaced).
rules.why: MCP clients may namespace tool names.

rules.rule: Pass exactly one of the single-id or multi-id parameters (style_id or style_ids, screen_id or screen_ids, flow_id or flow_ids).
rules.why: The parameter tables require exactly one.

rules.rule: Pass response_format (md or json) only when the client's tool schema includes it.

decisions.question: Which Refero research layer fits the question at hand?

options.name: Styles
options.effect: Gives visual direction and taste: colors, type, layout, elevation, do/don't rules
options.when: Brand feel, aesthetics, design-system inspiration, visual polish

options.name: Screens
options.effect: Shows concrete page structure, components, hierarchy, copy and states

options.name: Flows
options.effect: Shows step-by-step journey logic across connected screens
options.when: Onboarding, checkout, cancellation, upgrade, password reset and other sequences

decisions.recommendation: Styles first for taste, then screens and flows for product logic.

decisions.question: Return research in markdown or JSON?
decisions.recommendation: Use only when the client's tool schema exposes response_format.

process.detail: Run 3-5 refero_search_styles queries from different angles (broad aesthetic, domain, known brand); page through results.
Call refero_get_style on the promising UUIDs, 3-4 at most per batch.
Pick one primary foundation for mood and density, borrow 1-2 details from others, extract layout, component, spacing and elevation rules.
Use refero_search_screens with literal UI terms and a platform (web or ios); open strong hits with refero_get_screen and refero_get_similar_screens.
Use refero_get_screen_image only when metadata is not enough.
For journeys, use refero_search_flows then refero_get_flow for goals, actions, system responses and screens.
Map everything to the user's product, audience and constraints.
Broaden, drop adjectives, try adjacent categories or a known product, inspect later pages, rebuild sparse flows from screens.

caveats: This is product documentation for Refero's own MCP tools; it promotes Refero as the research source.
Tool names, parameters and coverage are tied to commit a9b54a3 and will change as the server changes.
Most content is tool-usage detail rather than design guidance; the transferable parts are the research method and reference-use rules.
